title: Kennedy Family Joins Lawsuit Against Trump’s Proposed Arch Near Arlington
dek: Nine members of the Kennedy family asked to join the legal challenge to a planned 250-foot arch, arguing it would cast a shadow over family graves at Arlington National Cemetery on Veterans Day.
author: Meridian Newsroom
keyPoints: Nine members of the Kennedy family filed court papers Tuesday to join the lawsuit against the arch, CBS News reported.
The family argues the 250-foot arch would block sightlines to the Kennedy gravesites and the Eternal Flame at the John F. Kennedy grave.
The lawsuit is brought by the District of Columbia and the Commonwealth of Virginia; several Vietnam War veterans are also suing.
The Justice Department had no comment on the filing, CBS said. President Trump is marking Veterans Day with a wreath-laying and remarks at Arlington National Cemetery, NBC News reported.
body:
Nine members of the Kennedy family have asked to join the legal challenge to President Donald Trump’s planned triumphal arch, arguing that it would cast a shadow over the graves of relatives and other service members at Arlington National Cemetery, [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/kennedy-family-trump-triumphal-arch/) reported.

## The filing

In court papers filed Tuesday, the family members, including children and grandchildren of Robert F. Kennedy and Sen. Ted Kennedy, argued that the arch would block the sightlines to the Kennedy gravesites and the Eternal Flame commemorating President John F. Kennedy. CBS reported that the three brothers, Robert F., Ted and John F. Kennedy, are buried at Arlington.

The family members seek to intervene as plaintiffs in the lawsuit brought by the District of Columbia and the Commonwealth of Virginia, CBS said. Several Vietnam War veterans are also suing the administration over the project.

## The project

The proposed arch, which CBS said is 250 feet tall, is slated for a traffic circle across the Potomac River from the Lincoln Memorial. The administration says it would commemorate 250 years of American independence and had sought to break ground as early as this month. Opponents, including local officials, congressional Democrats and some veterans, argue the administration did not follow the proper legal process and that it would block sightlines between the cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial, CBS reported.

## Veterans Day

Trump and Vice President JD Vance are marking Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery with a wreath-laying ceremony and remarks from the president, [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trump-administration/live-blog/trump-vance-veterans-day-congress-2026-election-live-updates-rcna608667) reported in its live coverage. A White House proclamation issued Nov. 10 marked the day.

## Other challenges

CBS News reported that several Vietnam War veterans are also suing the Trump administration over the arch. The District of Columbia and the Commonwealth of Virginia are plaintiffs in the case the Kennedy family seeks to join, and CBS said the Justice Department had no comment on the family’s filing.

## The family’s argument

In a statement, Rory Kennedy and Maxwell Kennedy said: “Americans from every corner of the country visit Arlington to honor those who served and sacrificed for our nation. A towering arch casting shadows across the graves of our father, mother, and uncles, as well as the graves of so many who have served our country, would also cast a shadow over our democratic principles,” CBS reported.

The family members also wrote that the project would “permanently cast a shadow over the graves of servicemen and women who made the ultimate sacrifice for this country.”

## Opposition and the administration’s case

CBS reported that local officials, congressional Democrats and some veterans and others with an interest in Arlington have pushed back on the project. Opponents argue the administration did not follow the proper legal processes, and warn that the arch would block sightlines between the cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial. The administration says the arch would commemorate 250 years of American independence.

The White House proclamation for Veterans Day, dated Nov. 10, said the Department of Veterans Affairs was restructuring to put veterans first and cited a record 3.1 million disability claims processed this year.
